answer_text:
Let

\[
I_n=\int_0^1 x^{2n}\sin\frac{\pi x}{2}\,dx.
\]

We want

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty} a_n I_n.
\]

We are given

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{a_n}{n}=\frac{2}{\pi},
\]

so

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{a_n}{2n}=\frac{1}{\pi}.
\]

Now estimate \(I_n\). Since \(x^{2n}\) becomes concentrated near \(x=1\) as \(n\to\infty\), and

\[
\sin\frac{\pi}{2}=1,
\]

we expect \(I_n\sim \frac{1}{2n}\).

Make this precise. The function

\[
f(x)=\sin\frac{\pi x}{2}
\]

is continuous on \([0,1]\) and \(f(1)=1\). Also,

\[
(2n+1)x^{2n}
\]

is a probability density on \([0,1]\), since

\[
\int_0^1 (2n+1)x^{2n}\,dx=1.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}(2n+1)\int_0^1 x^{2n}f(x)\,dx=f(1)=1.
\]

Thus,

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}(2n+1)I_n=1.
\]

Multiplying by \(\frac{2n}{2n+1}\to 1\), we get

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}2n I_n=1.
\]

Now write

\[
a_n I_n
=
\frac{a_n}{2n}\cdot 2n I_n.
\]

Taking limits,

\[
\lim_{n\to\infty} a_n I_n
=
\left(\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{a_n}{2n}\right)
\left(\lim_{n\to\infty}2n I_n\right)
=
\frac{1}{\pi}\cdot 1
=
\frac{1}{\pi}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{1}{\pi}}
\]
